Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Revisionist :- S.S. Rajput
Counsel for Opposite Party :- Govt. Advocate
Hon'ble Sudhir Agarwal,J.
1.

Heard Sri S.S. Rajput, Advocate, for revisionist and learned A.G.A. for State.
2. This Criminal Revision under Section 401 read with Section 397 Cr.P.C. has been filed aggrieved by judgment and order dated 30.11.1999 passed by 1st Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Aligarh in Case No. 207 of 1995 convicting and sentencing revisionist under Section 7/16 of Prevention of Food Adulteration Act, 1954 (hereinafter referred to as "Act, 1954").
Thereagainst accused-revisionist preferred Criminal Appeal No. 135 of 1999 which has been dismissed by 12th Additional Sessions Judge, Aligarh vide judgment and order dated 25.08.2000.
This revision has been filed challenging both the aforesaid orders.
3. Learned counsel for revisionist contended that there was violation of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 inasmuch report of Public Analyst was not served upon revisionist.

Before Trial Court, the case set up by prosecution is that analyst report was sent by registered post at the address of revisionist and that is how requirement of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 was satisfied and Trial Court has also treated the mere factum of sending analyst report by registered post to be sufficient compliance of Section 13(2) of Act, 1954 as is evident from following:

"P.W.-2 R.P. Gupta, Food Clerk, has in his statement verified the notice sent to the accused under Section 13 (2) of the P.F. Act and its postage receipt being exhibit Ka-11; and as regard sanction for prosecution, he has stated that the CMO, after having perused all the documents, dictated exhibit 8 sanction for prosecution.
The witness has identified the signature of the then CMO thereon.
In this way, the terms and conditions of Section 13(2) of the P.F. Act has been complied with and the notice has been received with the accused."
(English Translation by Court)
5. This aspect has also been confirmed in appeal.

6. However, I find that approach of Courts below with respect to compliance of Section 13(2) of Act is in the teeth of recent judgment of Supreme Court in Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019) (Arising out of S.L.P. (Criminal) No. 4314 of 2015) decided on 31.07.2019 wherein Court in para 15 of judgment said as under:
"The very purpose of furnishing such report is to enable the Accused to seek for reference to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis if the Accused is dissatisfied with the report.

entities.text: Vijendra Vs. State of U.P. and others (Criminal Appeal No. 1167 of 2019)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Such safeguard provided to the Accused Under Section 13(2) of the Act is a valuable right.

In that view even if the despatch of the report on 07.04.1980 is taken as substantial compliance though it is beyond the period of 10 days from 18.03.1980 i.e., the date on which the prosecution was lodged, in the absence of there being proof of delivery of the report to the Accused; in the instant facts the valuable right available to the Accused/Appellant to seek for reference within the period of 10 days stands defeated.
In that circumstance when the Appellant/Accused is made to suffer the penal consequences, it will have to be construed strictly.

In the facts and circumstances of this case, since as already noticed above the report of the Analyst has not in fact been served on the Appellant and the mere despatch of the report as per the statement of PW-2 was not sufficient."
(emphasis added)

7. Therefore, as a proposition of law, it cannot be doubted that prosecution, when challenged, must satisfy that notice issued under Section 13(2) has been served upon accused because it is right of Satya Deo Sharma vs State Of U.P. on 14 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/18053450/
2

entities.text: Satya Deo Sharma vs State Of U.P.
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: accused
and prosecution must prove that not only report of Public Analyst was sent by registered post, but it was actually served upon accused-Revisionist, which has not been done in the case in hand.
Impugned orders, therefore, cannot be sustained.
8. In the result, this revision is allowed.
Impugned judgements and orders dated 30.11.1999 and 25.08.2000 are hereby set aside.
9. Certify this judgment to the lower Court immediately.
